reasoning_content: Interesting point — in the grep results of docker-compose.yml, only the health checks for postgres, rabbitmq, and redis show up. But `docker compose ps` is reporting all 20 containers as healthy. Which means the app service health checks must be defined somewhere else — probably inside each service's Dockerfile (HEALTHCHECK). Let me check the sign-tool container's internal port, and try checking the Dockerfile's HEALTHCHECK.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "docker exec workspace-sign-tool-1 sh -c 'command -v node curl 2>/dev/null; echo \"---\"; node -e \"fetch(\\\"http://localhost:3000/test/ping\\\").then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>console.log(\\\"ping:\\\",t)).catch(e=>console.log(\\\"ERR\\\",e.message))\" 2>&1' | tail -3", "description": "Test sign-tool health from inside container", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Ping sign-tool inside its container"}
